STEP 1 - Scene: A lunch-style plate of mixed salad greens (spinach and mixed leaves with some red onion or dressing), kidney beans, and roasted potato cubes, photographed from above at a slight angle on a glass-topped table.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white square plate is roughly 26 cm across, so area ≈ 3.14 × (13)² ≈ 530 cm². Food covers roughly 60% of the plate.

STEP 3 - Items:
- Mixed leafy greens (spinach and mixed leaves, lightly dressed)
- Kidney beans (about 12 beans)
- Roasted potato cubes (about 5 pieces)

STEP 4 - Area:
- Mixed leaves: ~30% of plate (≈160 cm²)
- Potato cubes: ~20% (≈105 cm²)
- Kidney beans: ~8% (≈40 cm²)
- Total covered ≈ 58%, consistent with the visible coverage.

STEP 5 - Volume:
- Leaves: 160 cm² × 3 cm ≈ 480 ml (outer envelope)
- Potatoes: 105 cm² × 2 cm ≈ 210 ml
- Beans: 40 cm² × 1.5 cm ≈ 60 ml

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Leaves: 480 ml × 0.15 ≈ 72 g
- Potatoes: 210 ml × 0.7 ≈ 147 g
- Beans: 60 ml × 0.9 ≈ 54 g (cooked beans are dense)

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Leaves: 72 g × 23 kcal/100 g ≈ 17 kcal
- Potatoes (roasted, cooked weight): 147 g × 150 kcal/100 g ≈ 220 kcal (roasting in oil adds energy, so this is a moderate estimate)
- Kidney beans (cooked): 54 g × 127 kcal/100 g ≈ 69 kcal
- Total ≈ 306 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 270 g of food across a half-to-two-thirds covered plate is plausible. The total of roughly 300 kcal fits a side-salad-plus-potatoes lunch portion. Dressing is not clearly visible, so it is not added.
